全美航班大停飛：非關天災的系統浩劫

初步調查顯示，這場混亂並非遭受網路攻擊，而是阿肯色州航管設施包商在進行設備更新時，將老舊銅線更換為光纖並安裝新路由器，意外在通訊骨幹引發異常流量，每4至5秒便湧入約1,000次連線請求，直接使老舊設備失穩，迫使當局全面停飛以確保飛安。

系統老舊與邊飛邊換：現代化升級的三大盲點

第三則是現代化升級缺乏整合排程。美國政府問責署（GAO）曾警告，上萬個升級項目缺乏整合主進度表，重複施工與協調不足大幅增加了中斷風險，且FAA現場監管人員在測試後不久便爆發通訊異常，凸顯內部監督機制失靈。作者強調，航管脆弱性非美國獨有，英國近期亦曾因毫秒級的系統故障衝擊逾2,000架航班，顯示航管系統複雜度已高到牽一髮動全身。

面對航空客運量持續攀升、預估今年突破7,000萬人次的大關，台灣交通部也宣布將於八年內投入近192億元新台幣，全面推動航管設備與決策支援系統的數位現代化。作者表示，台灣目前航管系統採南北雙中心互相備援，能於主要系統異常時即刻接手；隨著台灣成為美加與東南亞間的重要國際轉運樞紐，穩健安全的航管系統將是維持全球競爭力的核心基石。

The affected area was widespread . While this didn't mean all planes in the air lost contact—some radios and radar were still functional—the president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association said controllers still had to follow emergency procedures to guide the 3,500 planes then in the.

air to land. The equipment upgrade that caused this nationwide aviation chaos was originally intended to make the U.S. aviation system safer and more stable. maintain operations or may become difficult to maintain in the future. You might think, "If the equipment is that old, just replace it quickly!" But is it really that simple? Think about it: if your home internet needs an upgrade, you can deal with an hour of downtime, but the national air traffic control system can't just shut down for three months to replace all its equipment. Right, moving on. So, the FAA has to keep planes flying normally while gradually replacing copper wires with fiber optics and swapping out routers. paths that affected over 100 air traffic control facilities nationwide. In short, the FAA has announced a suspension of the deployment of these new routers while waiting for... No. Don't think that only the U.S. has these issues; this September, the UK's air navigation service provider also experienced a system failure. The entire event lasted only a few milliseconds, yet it impacted over 2,000 flights. This shows the problem isn't just outdated equipment; it's that aviation systems are becoming increasingly complex, where a small error in one spot can cascade. throughout the entire system. What about Taiwan? Does our aviation system have the ability to withstand a similar crisis? In fact, Taiwan is also facing the challenge of upgrading air traffic control equipment. This October, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications announced plans to invest nearly 19.2 billion NT dollars over eight years to modernize equipment, including flight traffic management, digital voice communication, intelligent decision-support systems, and regional air traffic facilities. Why do we need to replace them? In addition to aging.

equipment, Taiwan's air traffic volume continues to increase. According to Civil Aeronautics Administration statistics, passenger numbers reached 64 million in 2024 and 68.89 million in 2025, with projections to exceed 70 million this year. Taiwan is not unprepared for such failures; current air traffic management systems are located in both the north and south to support each other. There is also a backup system that can take over flight services if the main system encounters a major anomaly. I am. actually quite glad to see Taiwan paying attention to this issue. I just flew back from Bali yesterday, and many passengers on the same flight were transiting through Taiwan to the US, Canada, and other places. Taiwan is becoming a preferred transit hub for more international travelers, so having excellent airport systems is one of our competitive edges globally. Alright, to wrap things up today, I'd like to ask everyone: if an airline told you your flight was delayed not because of the weather, but because of a glitch in the air traffic control system, would you be even angrier? 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入探討現代社會「毛孩家人化」趨勢，以及失去寵物時常面臨的「剝奪性悲傷」與社會不理解。
  • 解析台韓等國爆紅的線上寵物紀念網站，如何扮演虛擬心靈避風港，並分析其在療癒與引發「強迫性悲傷」間的心理機制。

摘要

線上寵物紀念平台的崛起與熱潮

作者指出，近年來虛擬寵物悼念平台在社群網絡上引發廣大迴響。由紐西蘭工程師為紀念已故愛犬創立的「L」網站，上線不久便吸引近百個國家、超過兩萬隻寵物進駐，其中台灣飼主建立的紀念頁面更佔了四成，點亮逾四十萬盞虛擬蠟燭；南韓的「StarCook」平台亦在十天內湧入三十二萬人次，甚至進一步結合流浪動物認養與協尋功能。這些宛如線上寵物靈骨塔的空間，讓飼主能透過點燭、獻花、寫信與虛擬互動，傾訴對離世毛孩的無盡思念。

毛孩家人化與難以言說的「剝奪性悲傷」

現代人與寵物的羈絆日益深厚，以台灣為例，犬貓數量已正式超越十四歲以下兒童人口。研究顯示，有超過兩成的受訪者認為失去寵物的痛楚甚至超越失去人類親友，許多人更出現長期的寵物失落症候群。然而，這種巨大的悲慟在現實中常被旁人輕描淡寫地忽視，形成心理學上所謂的「剝奪性悲傷」。因為缺乏社會的同理與認可，飼主往往感到孤立且羞於啟齒，這也是線上紀念社群成為他們安全釋放情感、尋求同理關鍵場所的原因。

社群療癒效益與潛在的「強迫性悲傷」

研究表明，線上哀悼社群能為飼主提供情感宣洩與相互支持的管道，實踐心理學所倡導的「持續性連結」，意即健康的面對悲傷不需完全遺忘，而是學會在缺席中建立新的心靈連結。然而，研究同時警告群體悼念可能伴隨「強迫性悲傷」的風險，讓參與者誤以為必須時刻保持痛苦才能證明對毛孩的愛。因此，專家建議健全的紀念空間應適度引導使用者在追思與回歸日常生活中找到健康平衡。

AI 科技重塑哀悼歷程的慰藉與反思

隨著人工智慧日新月異，AI 寵物紀念技術已能重現逝去毛孩的動態影像，甚至模擬其聲音與飼主對話或寫信。儘管這項技術為悲痛的飼主帶來即時的溫暖慰藉，但專家與學術界也示警其潛在的心理與倫理風險。過度逼真的互動恐讓飼主產生心理依賴、深陷科技幻象，進而難以接受毛孩已經離開的事實。部分開發者因而主動設立機制，鼓勵使用者適時從平台「畢業」，引領人們重新思考科技究竟是幫助療癒心靈，還是阻礙了哀悼歷程的自然前行。

================================================

It became an instant hit upon launch, with thousands of pet memorial pages from Taiwan created in under two weeks; many grieving owners say it makes them cry uncontrollably. More and more people now treat pets as family, and the pain of losing a pet is often just as intense as losing a human relative. In recent years, online pet memorial platforms have proliferated, and with AI becoming so advanced, even deceased pets can interact with their owners, but can these sites really help owners heal? Or do they just make it impossible to move on? Hello everyone, I’m Fan Chi-fei , welcome to Fan Chi-fei’s Special.

Report. Let’s take a look at what "L" is actually doing. Simply put, this website is like an online columbarium for pets. Users can control a small virtual avatar to wander around the site, reserve a spot for their pet who has crossed the Rainbow Bridge, or click on other pets ' photos to read the messages left by their owners. Anyone can light a candle or leave flowers for a pet they don't know, share words of comfort, or send small gifts like a can of food, a birthday cake, or. a toy; the site even features diary and sky lantern functions. The site sparked a massive trend immediately after its launch. The founder, MCH, an engineer based in New Zealand, says he originally wanted to create a 3D memorial for his dog, Bella , who passed away in 2020 at the age of 18. He mentioned that after Bella passed , no one in the family dared to speak her name because the pain was just too great. Later, he shared Bella's story online,.

and strangers left comments saying these stories helped them cope with their own loss, but he eventually worried that his memories were fading, so he decided to write them down—which inspired him to create this site to encourage others to express their grief. Since the site went live on November 1st , the founder promoted it in various languages on Threads, and it quickly went viral. According to platform statistics, as of now, nearly 100. countries and over 21,000 pets reside here. Among them, more than 8,400 pets are from Taiwan, accounting for 40%. Friends in Taiwan have lit over 400,000 candles on the platform, the highest number globally. A website that recently went viral in South Korea is called StarCook. That’s the site. According to Yonhap News, the platform launched on October 30th and accumulated approximately 320,000 visits in just 10 days. Initially, there were only 500 virtual memorial cabinets, which later.

expanded to nearly 22,000. The developer is an office worker in his 30s. He also lost two beloved cats and wanted to create a place to preserve memories, never expecting it to resonate so deeply . Beyond basic features like posting photos, writing letters, and lighting candles, this website even lets your virtual avatar walk and interact with your furry friend. Most notably, the platform recently began collaborating with animal welfare groups to establish a dedicated area for people to meet stray animals waiting for homes. There is also space for pet-finding notices,. allowing this space—originally meant for emotional comfort—to help animals in the real world that need care. In recent years, similar services have sprung up like mushrooms. Taiwan also launched "Nian-Nian Memorial " this year and "Eternal Dream Planet" in October; both focus on companionship , so you don't have to be alone. This. There are several directions to discuss regarding the popularity of such online pet memorial sites. First, the.

humanization of pets. The relationship between modern people and pets is very different from before. A 2023 survey by the Pew Research Center found that 97%of pet owners consider their pets part of the family, and 51% consider them as important as other human family members. Official surveys released in South Korea also show that about 30%of households own pets. What about here in Taiwan? As mentioned previously in "Small Inventions, Big Revolutions," one in every four households in Taiwan owns a pet. According to 2025 official statistics,. the total number of pet dogs and cats in Taiwan has exceeded 3.2 million, surpassing the number of children under 14. In other words, there are more pets than children. Second, the grief of losing a furry friend may be far more severe than we imagine. A study published in an international journal this January surveyed nearly 1,000 British adults. It found that among respondents who had experienced the deaths of both pets and human loved ones , 21%felt the loss of their pet was more devastating and painful. Many even met.

the criteria for prolonged grief disorder, meaning their sorrow lasted a long time and severely impacted their daily lives. Korean society is also increasingly recognizing "pet loss syndrome," where pet owners experience intense grief and a sense of profound loss after the passing of their beloved companion. In psychology, there is a term called "disenfranchised grief," which occurs when a person's sorrow is not understood or validated by society— something that frequently happens to pet owners. Losing a furry companion is painful enough, but those who don't understand might say, "It’s just a dog,. you can always get another one!" If anyone said that to me, I’d fight them. Even taking time off work can be dismissed as making a mountain out of a molehill. A 2021 analysis found that bereaved pet owners often feel isolated and are even embarrassed to express their grief. Other studies interviewing animal caregivers have also discovered that when grief goes unrecognized, the individuals involved are more likely to fall into isolation. So, the significance of online pet memorial sites may not just be to commemorate our furry friends, but to finally provide these "parents" a place where they can.

grieve safely, without fear of being mocked. Third, do online memorial spaces actually have a healing effect? Just this April, researchers in South Korea published a study on this topic. After interviewing 18 users of online pet bereavement communities, they found that respondents felt these groups helped them express their sadness, receive understanding, and find mutual support from others with similar experiences. However, the study also identified an unexpected issue called "compulsory grief." This means that when a group spends. every day reminiscing about departed pets, it can make some participants feel they must remain sad to prove they still love them. The researchers therefore suggest that effective online memorial sites should help users find a balance between mourning their pets and re-engaging with daily life. In psychology, there is a concept called "continuing bonds." Healthy grieving doesn't require us to completely forget the deceased, but rather to learn how to maintain a new type of emotional relationship in their.

absence. So, occasionally lighting a candle or looking at photos of a late cat or dog doesn't mean you haven't moved on; the point is to observe whether doing so helps you. It’s a step forward. Fourth, technology has made the grieving process more complex. Now, AI can not only recreate the likeness of a pet that has passed away but can even simulate interactions with their owners. For example, a Japanese owner took an old photo of their Shiba Inu from 44 years ago and. used AI to make the dog move again. In the video, the Shiba Inu not only turns its head but also tilts it toward the camera, as if it had truly returned to its owner's side. AI also provides a " letter from your pet" feature. In China , DEPS uses the pet's information and the owner's current feelings to simulate the pet's voice and write new letters, allowing owners to even write back and continue communicating. You know perfectly well that it wasn't really written by a dog, but as you read those details that only the two of you knew, you can't help but shed a tear, right?

Is this truly a form of comfort, or just an illusion manufactured by technology? A Japanese company launched the PETMemoryAI service, where owners can upload photos and personality traits of deceased pets to generate videos of them , or even chat with their owners in the pet's own "voice." However, this company is also worried about owners becoming too dependent on AI. They designed the system to avoid frequent notifications and even encourages users to eventually "graduate" from the platform, meaning to say goodbye to their virtual pet. Since. the boom in AI technology, haven't some people already started using AI to bring back deceased loved ones? This has always been a major controversy. Research from the University of Cambridge warns that this type of AI, which mimics individuals, could pose serious psychological and ethical risks . Looking back at pets, when AI allows us to constantly reunite with our deceased furry friends, is it really healing our grief, or is it making us more reliant on AI for solace, making it even harder to accept the fact that they are gone?
